subject: Penetration test report sharing conditions & redaction criteria
messages:
From: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@fintech.co>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: full penetration test report under NDA

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the helpful SOC 2 scope overview last week. Our security team has a parallel request: they would like to review the latest penetration test report for Redwood's platform (the engagement you completed in May).

We understand full reports are sensitive — we're prepared to sign an NDA. Can you please confirm:
- Whether you can share the full report (not just the exec summary) under NDA?
- Your redaction policy (what you typically remove: PII, internal hostnames, exploit POC code, timelines, vendor names, etc.)
- Expected turnaround once NDA is in place?

Our security lead (copied) is Tom Greene from VendorSec; he can take the technical discussion. If you prefer, we can sign a mutual NDA via DocuSign.

Appreciate a quick outline so we can slot this into our vendor review timeline.

Best,
Alicia Ramos
VP, InfoSec — FinTechCo

Attachment: vendor-sig-request-form.pdf (form filled)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@fintech.co>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: full penetration test report under NDA

Hi Alicia — thanks for the note and for attaching the VendorSec form.

Short answer: we can share a redacted full report under a signed NDA. A couple of constraints and options so expectations are aligned:

1) What we can share
- Fully redacted full report (detailed findings with exploit POCs scrubbed)
- Executive summary (we can share an unredacted exec summary covering high-level risk ratings)
- Remediation evidence (patch notes, vulnerability scanner exports, test verification screenshots)

2) Typical redactions
- Exploit proof-of-concept code and step-by-step exploit sequences
- Internal hostnames, private IPs, and environment-specific identifiers
- Any sampled customer data or credentials
- Vendor-internal operational runbooks

3) Process & timeline
- We require a signed mutual NDA before transfer (DocuSign link below).
- Once NDA is executed and redaction scope is agreed, we can produce a redacted report within 3 business days.
- For targeted follow-up questions we can schedule a 60-minute walkthrough with our security engineer.

Dev — can you draft the redaction checklist and confirm what remediation artifacts we can attach? Evelyn — please coordinate Legal (Laura) for NDA review; I will prepare the secure transfer link (SFTP with 7-day TTL).

Link: https://docusign.net/REDWOOD-PT-NDA-2026

Best,
Hannah
Head of Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Thanks Hannah — quick technical note on redactions and artifacts we can provide:

Redaction candidates (we can automate/remove):
- POC snippets that contain exploit payloads/commands: yes, remove.
- Repro steps that include private CIDR hostnames: redact hostnames and replace with generalized labels (e.g., "internal-host-1").
- Screenshots that show customer email addresses: blur.

Remediation evidence we can attach:
- Post-fix vulnerability scan export (Nessus/Qualys CSV) — confirms CVE closure dates
- Patch/commit links (internal commit ids redacted) — we can provide the commit message and public PR link where applicable
- Test verification notes from our infra team (screenshotstamped)

Packaging: we can produce a ZIP with: redacted-report.pdf (PDF stub for sharing), remediation-evidence-YYYYMMDD.zip, and a short tech memo mapping finding IDs to evidence items.

I will prepare redaction-guidelines-v1.docx and share to Hannah's secure transfer.

- Dev
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@fintech.co>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: full penetration test report under NDA (NDA redline)

Hi all — legal here. I reviewed the DocuSign template Alicia sent and uploaded a redlined version to DocuSign (link below). High level redline notes:

- We prefer a mutual NDA (not one-way) with a 3-year term.
- Exclude non-actionable, aggregated vulnerability metrics from confidentiality so the parties can discuss aggregate risk publicly.
- Carveout for required disclosures (law enforcement/regulatory requests) with notice to Redwood where permitted.
- Add an explicit prohibition on sublicensing or transferring the report to third parties without Redwood's written consent.

If FinTechCo accepts the redline, we will countersign in DocuSign and proceed with redaction + secure transfer.

DocuSign link: https://docusign.net/REDWOOD-PT-NDA-2026 (redlined)

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
